content.seo_title: Sell Your Junk Car in Henderson, NV | {business}
content.seo_description: We buy junk, damaged and non-running vehicles across Henderson. Free towing, a firm offer, and payment at pickup. Call {phone} for a number in minutes.
content.hero_heading: We Buy Junk Cars Across Henderson — Running or Not
content.hero_description: Damaged, dead, or simply finished. Tell us what is sitting there and you get a firm cash offer, free towing to wherever it is parked, and payment the moment we collect it.

sections.heading: Why Henderson Vehicle Owners Call Us
paragraphs: Most of the vehicles we collect in Henderson stopped being worth the next repair a while ago. A transmission that costs more than the car, an emissions failure with a list of parts behind it, something inherited that nobody in the house wants to drive. We buy them running or not, damaged or complete, and the condition never disqualifies a vehicle from an offer.

What you are quoted is what you are paid. The offer is firm once it is made, there are no fees taken off it at collection, and towing is included rather than deducted. Payment happens at pickup, not at some point afterwards.

One thing worth knowing if you are in Henderson specifically: the city is incorporated and enforces its own property maintenance and nuisance code through its own code enforcement office, separately from Clark County. For some owners that turns a someday job into one with a deadline attached, which is the subject further down this page.

sections.heading: Henderson Puts a Number On How Many You Can Keep
paragraphs: Henderson's property maintenance code limits how many inoperable or unregistered vehicles a property may keep, and the limit is tied to the property's zoning designation rather than applied as one flat figure across the city. Properties in an RNP-1 designated area are allowed up to six. RNP-2 areas are allowed up to four. Every other property is limited to two.

Two conditions sit alongside that count, and both are narrower than people assume. Vehicles that are permitted must be screened by a substantially opaque fence at least six feet high — screening is a condition on vehicles already within the number, not a way to keep an extra one out of sight. And the city allows a single inoperable vehicle registered to a resident of the property and undergoing minor repair work, for a period not exceeding 72 hours.

If that puts you over, there are two ways back: build to the standard, or reduce the count by one. Selling the vehicle that has not moved in years is usually the shorter road, and it is the only one that also clears the space.

content.faq_heading: Questions Henderson Residents Ask Before Selling

faq.question: Do you buy vehicles that do not run at all?
faq.answer: Yes. We buy vehicles running or not, damaged or complete. A car that will not start, will not hold a charge, or has not moved in years is the ordinary case rather than the exception, and towing is free either way.

faq.question: How many inoperable vehicles can I legally keep in Henderson?
faq.answer: It depends on your property's zoning designation. RNP-1 areas are allowed up to six, RNP-2 areas up to four, and every other property is limited to two. Henderson enforces this itself, separately from Clark County, so a county figure is not the one that applies at a Henderson address.

faq.question: If I build a fence, can I keep one more?
faq.answer: No. Screening by a substantially opaque fence at least six feet high is a condition placed on vehicles that are already within the permitted number. It is not a way to exceed the count.

faq.question: What if I do not have the title?
faq.answer: Tell us on the call. It is a common situation and we can often still help, though it depends on the circumstances. Raising it early is better than discovering it on the doorstep.

final_cta.heading: Get an Offer on Your Henderson Vehicle
final_cta.intro: Tell us what you have and where it is parked. We will handle the rest.

local_conditions.materially_affects: Establishes that the business serves the area at all.

local_conditions.condition: Under NRS 116.3102 a Nevada community association may cause a vehicle to be removed when it is improperly parked on property owned or leased by the association, or on a road, street, alley or other thoroughfare within the community. 48 hours' notice is required except for fire hydrants, fire lanes, accessible spaces, or an imminent threat to health, safety or welfare.
local_conditions.materially_affects: Sets the boundary of what an association can actually do. A vehicle on the owner's own driveway is outside this power, which is the opposite of what the live page implies.

local_conditions.condition: Under NRS 116.31031, a fine for a violation not posing an imminent threat may not exceed $100 per violation or $1,000 per hearing, a hearing opportunity is required, and a violation uncured after 14 days may draw an additional fine for each subsequent 7-day period.
local_conditions.materially_affects: This is the real enforcement pressure — fines through a process with a cure window, not daily penalties and not towing from a driveway.

local_conditions.condition: NRS 116 applies to common-interest communities throughout Nevada, not to Henderson specifically.
local_conditions.materially_affects: Decisive for differentiation: a statutory regime shared by every sibling area cannot distinguish one location page from another.

local_conditions.condition: Henderson Municipal Code § 15.12.030 B.3 caps inoperable or unregistered vehicles per property by zoning designation (six RNP-1, four RNP-2, two elsewhere), requires screening by a substantially opaque six-foot fence, and allows a single resident-registered vehicle under minor repair for no more than 72 hours.
local_conditions.materially_affects: It is the countable rule a Henderson owner is measured against, and it converts a vague worry into a decision with a number attached.
